kicker: Real estate · H1 pre-sales vs FY27 guidance, Q2 FY27
title: 6 of 11 developers are on pace for FY27 sales goals
dek: Most booked the usual ~40% of their full-year pre-sales target by September; Brigade and DLF trail. Nifty Realty rose 1.55% on 20 Nov, but with CPI at 6.09%, rate relief may wait, so H2 launches must carry the targets.

read: Demand is tracking plans at most developers, but every target is H2-weighted, so approval and launch timing, not buyers, is the main risk to FY27 numbers.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Nifty Realty: HDFC Sky, 20 Nov 2026; CPI: Liquide, 13 Nov 2026
notes: Pre-sales (the value of homes booked in the period) is used instead of reported revenue, because developers book revenue only when projects are completed or handed over, so revenue swings with delivery dates: Embassy Developments' Q2 revenue fell 41% in the quarter its pre-sales hit a record, and Godrej Properties' Q2 income rose 38% while bookings fell 6%. Each bar is H1 FY27 pre-sales divided by the FY27 pre-sales target, both as stated on the Q2 call (midpoint where a range was given; Arvind SmartSpaces' guide was raised on the call to ₹2,600–2,700 crore; Godrej's 43% is as stated by management, since its call gave only an H2 range). DLF's H1 adds Q1 bookings of ₹657 crore and Q2 of about ₹3,800 crore from the two calls, against the ₹20,000 crore target from its Q1 call, which management only 'hopes' to hold; Brigade's H1 is the top of the stated ₹2,888–2,900 crore range. Growth figures are as stated and mix H1 and Q2 bases; Signatureglobal and DLF gave none. Sri Lotus (46% of its guide, H1 +176%) and Suraj Estate (50%, H1 +48%) are also ahead of pace but left off the chart for space. Left out: Sobha, Mahindra Lifespace, Oberoi and Kolte-Patil (no Q2 call in our data), Phoenix Mills (malls), Sunteck, Raymond Realty and Runwal (guide given only as growth or a loose range), Ajmera and Arkade (target ambiguous or cited only by an analyst), and Aditya Birla Real Estate (declined to guide). News hook: Nifty Realty rose 1.55% on 20 Nov 2026 (HDFC Sky); October CPI was 6.09%, above the RBI's tolerance band (Liquide, 13 Nov 2026), and Lodha's call noted a 25 bp repo hike in October, with mortgage-dependent buyers of ₹1–5 crore homes the most sensitive.
